items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: I remember the first Goodman record that had any real wide circulation... was a record of Sometimes I'm Happy, in which Arthur Rolini played a tenor solo... These were the two records that really made the first big impression.

ctx.x: Well, the other musicians from New Orleans, it was kind of a convenient hangout, and Sharky

used to cook for us occasionally, Creole. And that's where I met Shields, and then in the same group of musicians, but in another place I met quite frequently Tony Parenti. And again, at the time he was considered pretty bad, pretty corny. In fact, I jammed with him in the apartment, and that was my impression of him. But he's still going pretty strong right now, as you know. And I thought of him as an old man then. When did you move to New York? It would be 1934, even 1933 possibly, as soon as I got out of high…
And George Van Epps and the Guitar Tealers was another big thing in that record to me.
